Surah 45: al-Jathiyah, also called ash-Shari'ah.

Its purpose is to show that the One who sent down this Book, as was indicated at the beginning of al-Dukhan, is "Possessor of Might" (dhu al-'izzah), because nothing overcomes Him while He overcomes everything; and "Possessor of Wisdom" (al-hikmah), because He never places anything except in its most fitting place. Thus it is known that He alone is characterized by Greatness (al-kibriya'), so He has laid down a law (shar') that is in the utmost uprightness, which the intellects cannot fully grasp by themselves and from which nothing falls outside. In it He commands and forbids, and gives hope and instills fear. Then it is hidden (batana) to the extent that it cannot be recognized, and then it is manifest to the extent that it cannot be unknown. Among the accountable are those who subject their intellect to judgment, turn away from their desires, witness His majesty, hear and obey; and among them are those who follow their desires, stray from the light of reason, go astray and are lost. Wisdom therefore requires, and it must be so, that Glorified is He gather the creation for the Day of Decision (yawm al-fasl), so that He may be manifest in every respect, and requite His servants, so that the obedient may witness His mercy and the disobedient His greatness, and so that He may spread justice, display grace, and manifest Himself in all His attributes to all His creatures. Upon this the name of the surah, ash-Shari'ah, points, and its name al-Jathiyah has clear indication in it, when each of its two verses is pondered. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is the Guide.

"In the name of Allah" (bismillah), who alone has perfect might and greatness; "the Most Gracious" (al-Rahman), who has perfected His mercy through general clarification for the happy and the wretched; "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahim), who has singled out the friends (awliya') with the garments of His obedience.

* *

﴿Ha-Mim﴾ That is: the wisdom of Muhammad (ﷺ) is its ultimate end, as has preceded in al-Dukhan, which indicated the sending down of it from the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab) all at once to the House of Might (bayt al-'izzah), and it indicated its blessing by means of what indicated the wisdom of its Sender and His might, through glad tidings and warning, the striking of the criminals after long forbearance and patience, the salvation of the God-fearing, and other matters which are in the utmost indication of that, because they return to goodness for whoever gives ear while being a witness. He pointed to its ease for whoever ponders this Reminder, translated into the tongue of the highest of creation, the most perfect and most noble of them in character and the most excellent of them. He began this [surah] by informing that He increased that ease and facility by sending it down in installments according to events, corresponding to them in the most perfect correspondence, after its sending down in its entirety from the Mother of the Book, and then arranged what was sent down from it in an arrangement that conveys sciences and clarifies hidden, important secrets. So He said:

Revelation of the Book (tanzīl al-kitāb): that is, the sending down of the one that gathers every good, sent down in parts (mufarraqan) to ease understanding and to convey clearly with facility in teaching, along with other abundant bounty.

He increased its greatness by saying: "from Allah" (min Allāh), that is, it is from the One encompassing all attributes of perfection.

Since, as has passed, honor (al-ʿizza) and wisdom (al-ḥikma) carry the greatest blessing here, He said: "the Almighty, the All-Wise" (al-ʿazīz al-ḥakīm). So His Book is mighty and wise, not as the disbelievers say, that it is poetry, or lies, or soothsaying; for there is no wisdom in that nor any might such that its matter could be confused with the matter of this Book, which encompasses the circle of wisdom and correctness. He indicated, through the signs of power and the traces of craftsmanship in the copy of this Book, both attributes and His oneness in them, from which follows His absolute uniqueness. He said this emphatically on account of those who deny it, even if by their deeds, and to encourage careful reflection by contemplating the signs of existence, of which this Book is an explanation of their obscure parts and a detailing of their summarized parts, and an indication that they are fit to turn thoughts toward contemplating them.

﴿Indeed, in﴾ When the Ḥawāmīm (the suras beginning with *ḥā-mīm*), as Abū ʿUbayda reported in *Kitāb al-Faḍāʾil* from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, are the essence (*lubāb*) of the Qur'an, He omitted what was mentioned in al-Baqara in His words "created," so that what is mentioned here would be more comprehensive. He said: ﴿the heavens﴾, meaning their very selves, with what they contain of indication (*dalāla*) [to their Maker] and Creator, with the lessons in them, with their benefits and their great craftsmanship, and with their eminence, which indicates their multiplicity through the stars in them. ﴿And the earth﴾, likewise, [and] with what it holds of minerals, means of livelihood, springs, and resources. ﴿Are signs﴾, meaning proofs of His oneness and of the totality of His perfection, for it is known that each of these must have a Maker characterized by that. ﴿For those who believe﴾, meaning: because they, by their firm establishment in this noble attribute, are fit for reflection, since their Lord guides them by their faith. So the witnesses of His lordship are clear to them in both, and the proofs of His divinity are manifest in them. Perhaps by expressing it with the description [of being believers], he indicated that in refuting the doubts of the naturalists (*ahl al-ṭabāʾiʿ*) one must first have faith, and that whoever is not firmly grounded in faith will not be freed from their doubts.

Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr said: When the preceding sura included clarification of the matter of the Book, the greatness of its exposition, and that it is a sufficient cure, a guidance, and a light, the matter of those among the Arabs who disbelieved became the greatest thing, because of their incapacity and inability, and because the proof was established against them, to the point that they accepted killing and immediate disgrace, yet they did not undertake to claim that they could produce its equal, nor did they aspire to attribute to themselves anything of the magnitude of such a counter-challenge. Then He, exalted is He, followed that with an admonition to His Prophet and the believers regarding the other proofs He had set up, which turn away from consideration of them, or from some of them, the one who is averse only his own desire, and who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah. So after swearing by the Manifest Book, the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾, meaning: even if you, O Muhammad, had not brought them the great sign of the Book, there would have been for them, in what We have set up of proofs, the greatest demonstration and the greatest exposition. ﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term﴾ [al-Rūm: 8]. When He alerted them by the creation of the heavens and the earth, He followed with mention of what He scattered in the earth, saying:

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 4:**

﴿And in your creation and what He scatters of living creatures are signs for a people who have certainty.﴾ ﴿And the alternation of night and day﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 5] That is: in the entering of one of them upon the other with the finest connection and the tightest separation. ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40] (p-63) Then He drew attention to reflection upon the sending down of water from the sky, and called it provision by way of a lesser analogy, so He said: ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and with it revives the earth after its death﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 5]. Then He said: ﴿And the turning of the winds are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 5]. Drawing inferences from these verses requires an extended elaboration. Then He said: ﴿These are the signs of Allah which We recite to you in truth﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6], that is, His indications and His proofs. ﴿And there is not a thing but it glorifies Him with His praise﴾ [al-Isra': 44]. Then He said: ﴿So in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6]. The most remote of what they have witnessed is the witness of the Book and what the creation of the heavens and the earth includes, and what is in them and between them, of wondrous clear proofs for people of understanding. So if they do not take heed from any of that, then by what will they take heed? Then Exalted is He followed this with a rebuke and reproach for their obstinacy despite the clarity of the matter, so He said: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 7], through the three verses. Then He said: ﴿This is guidance﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 11], and He referred to the Book and made it the very essence of guidance, because it bears all the causes of guidance and all its aspects. Then He threatened whoever disbelieves in it (p-64). Then He followed that with mention of His blessings and favours, so that this would add to their reproach. The verses were joined together, supporting this purpose through rebuke, reproach, warning and threat, until the end of the surah. End.

When He, glorified is He, had mentioned reflection upon the signs of the horizons, He followed them with the signs of the souls, so He said: ﴿And in your creation﴾, that is, the creation that differs from the creation of the earth from which you come, by choice, reason, mobility, and power over benefit and harm. ﴿And what He scatters﴾, that is, [spreads and] disperses by voluntary movement, scattering continuously and perpetually, ﴿of living creatures﴾, of what you know and what you do not know, with what is in that of your sharing with them in voluntary movement and in guidance toward benefits through perception of particulars, and your difference from them in form and reason and the perception of universals, and other differences in shapes, benefits, natures and the like. ﴿Are signs﴾ [that point] to the attributes of perfection, especially might and wisdom. In the recitation of Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub (the variant readings, qira'at, of these readers), it is in the accusative here, and in the one that follows, the two verses are conjoined to the sphere of "inna" (indeed) in the first verse, with its subject and predicate. Thus this verse has a regard toward emphasis. In the recitation of the majority, it is a nominative beginning by conjunction with "inna" and what is within its scope, and this is more eloquent, because it indicates that what is in the shaping of living beings and all their affairs of wondrous craftsmanship (p-65) is clearly indicative of Allah, [so] it is of such a nature that no one denies it, and so it is free of the need for emphasis. It is also permissible that the verse in the accusative reading is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device of mutual omission): he omitted "creation" in the first instance, indicated by what is mentioned in the second, and in the second he omitted "the essences of the souls," indicated by the "essences of the heavens" mentioned in the first.

Since the signs of the souls are more subtle and more indicative of power and choice through their renewal and variety, He said: ﴿for a people﴾, that is, among whom is the capacity to undertake what they strive for, ﴿who have certainty﴾, that is, for whom the ascent through the degrees of faith is continually renewed until they reach the nobility of certainty, so that no doubt mingles with them regarding His oneness. Al-Harali said in his tafsir (exegesis) of ﴿or like the one who passed by a town﴾ [al-Baqarah: 259]: the sign of the soul alerts to the sign of the senses, and the sign of the senses alerts to the sign of the soul, except that the sign of the soul is more intimate, and therefore it is more guiding. The ultimate of the sign of the horizons is faith, and the ultimate of the sign of the soul is certainty.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 45, verse 5:

When he mentioned the vessel (al-zarf) and the people for whose sake it was made, he joined to them some of what He created for their sake, because of their nobility through life. He followed this with what He placed in the vessel of conveniences for the sake of living creatures, and so He said: ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾, by the going of one of them and the coming of the other after its going, in succession, as a repeated sign pointing to the power to bring into being after annihilation, through resurrection and other things. The word "alternation" (ikhtilaf) is in the genitive by the implied preposition "fi" (in), so the conjunction takes the place of a single governing particle for the beginning (of the sentence) according to the one who reads "signs" (ayat) in the nominative, and takes the place of "inna" according to the one who reads it in the accusative. Thus it does not follow that it substitutes for two different governing particles at the beginning, in the nominative case, and for "inna" in the accusative case.

Since rain is more indicative than what has passed of resurrection and of might, because the more a thing is unfamiliar, the more it is possible to reflect upon it, He gave it precedence over them, and so He said: ﴿And what Allah sends down﴾, that is, the One whose greatness is complete, whose word is executed. Since sending down (inzal) may be used for what comes from a height in a figurative sense even if it is not physical, he clarified that both meanings are intended here, and so He said: ﴿from the sky﴾.

Since the benefits of the sky are not confined to water, He said: ﴿of provision﴾, that is, rain and other causes that prepare the emergence of provision, ﴿and He gives life thereby﴾, that is, by means of it and following it, ﴿to the earth﴾, that is, the one suitable for life. For this reason He said: ﴿after its death﴾, that is, its dryness, the shattering of the plants in it, and their turning into dust by mixing with its soil. When water descends upon it, it gathers it from the earth and brings it forth as it was, each time its descent is renewed. For this reason he did not use the preposition (i.e., "ba'd" in the construction of the verse with a different particle) to indicate the permanence of life in potential if not in actuality.

Since he mentioned what includes water, he mentioned the cause of the clouds which carry it, and so He said: ﴿and the turning of the winds﴾, in every direction of the cosmos and in every sense of mercy, punishment and other causes. He did not mention the ship and the clouds as in al-Baqarah, because of the requirement of the essence (lubabiyya) named by the Hawamim (the surahs beginning with ha mim). That is because they are among the benefits of the turning. The reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i (the plural "riyah" as singular "rih") is more eloquent, because the turning of one thing in many directions is more wondrous. ﴿Signs﴾: the reading in the nominative is more eloquent, as it indicates, by the absence of need for emphasis, that what is in the verse is plainly evident as proof of the Maker's power and choice through the alternation within the turning. Water, with what arises from it of growth, is clearer evidence of resurrection than the rest of them. Because of how clearly they appear, He attached the matter of them to reason, and so He said: ﴿for a people who use their reason﴾. Al-Qali said: the meaning is that the fair-minded, when they look at the heavens and the earth and recognize that they must have a Maker, believe; when they look at the creation of themselves and the like, their faith increases and they become certain; when they look at all other events, they understand and their knowledge becomes firm.

(p-68) When he had mentioned these magnificent signs, all of which share in greatness, and after he had indicated the differences in their ranks in obscurity and clarity through their endings (fawasil), he said, pointing to the loftiness of their rank by using the demonstrative of distance: ﴿Those﴾, i.e., the great signs, ﴿are the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., the proofs of the All-Encompassing (al-Muhit) possessing the attributes of perfection, than which nothing is more manifest, more evident, or more clear. Since it was as if it had been said, "What about them?", he said: Or the meaning is: We point to them while we ﴿recite them﴾, i.e., we follow up their narration, ﴿to you﴾, whether they are seen or heard, ﴿in truth﴾, i.e., a firm matter that cannot be altered, so it is neither magic nor falsehood. Thereupon, at that point, a rebuke of them follows, and of those who seek to comply with their demands for suggested miracles out of hope for their faith, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then in what statement﴾, i.e., in what great and true report whose knowledge is renewed for them and which deserves to be spoken of, ﴿after Allah﴾, i.e., the greatest report about the Sovereign Most High, ﴿and His signs﴾, i.e., and the report about His great indications, ﴿will they believe?﴾ Those who read in the address form, and they are the majority, returned it to His saying: "And in your creation" (45:4), and that is stronger in rebuke. The others, namely Abu 'Amr, Hafs from 'Asim, and Rawh from Ya'qub, held that this address was turned toward the address of the Prophet (ﷺ) in His saying: ﴿We recite them to you in truth﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 7:

Since no one would persist in disbelief to any degree after this clarification, except one who deserves punishment for openly defying with obstinacy, He said, drawing a conclusion and threatening: ﴿Woe﴾, i.e., a known place in Jahannam (Hellfire), ﴿to every lying sinner﴾, i.e., one who goes to great lengths in turning the truth away from its direction, ﴿sinful﴾, i.e., one who goes to great lengths in acquiring sin (ithm), which is wrongdoing, and doing what is not permitted of that which necessitates punishment. This is explained by His saying:

﴿He hears the signs of Allah﴾, that is, the manifest indications of the Supreme King, while they are ﴿recited﴾, that is, he continues to listen to them through the tongue of speech or of state, from whoever recites, ﴿being recited to him﴾ with all that they contain of ease of understanding, sweetness of wording, clarity of meanings, and grandeur of purposes, together with their miraculous nature. How much more so when the reciter is the noblest of creation.

Since their recitation necessitates his desisting, and his persistence, despite the extreme ugliness of his state, was something to be deemed improbable, He said: ﴿Then he persists﴾, that is, he continues, with a great persistence, in the foul thing he is engaged in, ﴿being arrogant﴾, that is, seeking arrogance and refusing to submit, and creating it for himself. And since, given what has been mentioned of his condition, it could be that he hears them, He lightened the severity of his disbelief by clarifying that they had no effect on him of any kind, so that his heart was harder than stone. [So He said]: ﴿as though﴾, that is, as though he ﴿had not heard them﴾. From this, and from the persistence and the restriction by arrogance, it is known that his state while hearing, before it, and after it is of one equal measure. By this description it is also known that every [one] whom the signs of Allah Most High do not turn back is one who exceeds in sin and falsehood, and so for him there is woe.

Since persistence means a dominating continuity, He did not mention the deafness (al-waqr), which is among the lasting ailments, as He mentioned it in Surat Luqman. Ibn al-QattA' and Ibn Zarif said in their books on verbs: asarra 'ala al-dhanb wa al-makruh means "he remained upon the sin and the disliked thing." Abd al-Ghafir al-Farisi said in al-Majma': asrartu 'ala al-shay', meaning I persisted and continued upon it. Ibn Faris said in al-Mujmal: al-israr is resolve upon a thing and steadfastness in it. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz said in his Diwan, quoting from Abd al-Haqq in his Wa'i: the root of al-sarr is holding fast, and from it one says: "So-and-so persisted upon such-and-such," meaning he remained upon it and held it fast within himself and bound himself to it, because he may say what is not in his heart and what he does not believe. "The man is musirr upon the sin," meaning he holds fast to it and firmly believes in it. Then [al-Qazzaz] said: from al-israr upon it, which is the resolve not to desist from it. Al-Asfahani, following the author of al-Kashshaf, said: its origin is from asarra al-himar 'ala al-anah, which is when the donkey bends over the female wild ass with its ears laid back (sarran udhunayhi).

Since He informed of his steadfastness in wickedness, He consequently made the threat for it in a style that indicates, by its mockery, the intensity of anger, and that if there is any glad tiding for him, it is punishment, so there is no glad tiding for him at all. So the Most High said: ﴿So give him tidings﴾, that is, for this wicked act, ﴿of a punishment﴾ that leaves in it no sweetness whatsoever, ﴿painful﴾, that is, of intense infliction.

When God, exalted is He, had made clear his disbelief through what he hears of the verses, He followed it with something more general than that, saying: ﴿And when he knows﴾, i.e., whatever kind of means of knowledge it may be, ﴿of Our verses﴾, i.e., with the greatness they possess by their being attributed to Us, ﴿anything﴾.

[وراءَهُ] And whenever they see that a person is wholly within their power, He says, explaining the punishment: ﴿Jahannam﴾, that is, it will take them without doubt, while they are in complete heedlessness of it through their neglect of guarding against it. The expression "behind" (warā') is fitting here because the discourse concerns the liar (al-affāk), and it is the turning of affairs away from their proper faces toward their backs. Such a person is always walking toward what is behind him, so he walks into the Fire with his back. The word warā' is also used to mean "in front" (al-imām); in that case it is a metaphor for encompassing, meaning: it will take them from the direction in which they know and from the direction in which they are ignorant, so it will meet them with extreme scowling, frowning, rage and aversion, the opposite of what they were upon when they knew the visible and audible signs, with the mocking that accompanies laughter and the swaggering in arrogance and insolence, and like what they were upon when they encountered those who affirmed those signs.

[و] Since they used to display their reliance on what was in their hands of transient accidental goods, He said: ﴿And will not avail them﴾, that is, in warding off that, ﴿what they earned﴾, that is, what they acquired of the things that brought them the honour which led them to mockery, ﴿anything﴾, that is, of sufficiency. And since these people, because of the blindness they are in, claim that their gods will suffice them, He said, stating it explicitly: ﴿nor what they took﴾, that is, what they obliged themselves to take, opposing what their original sound natures, free from distance from them, called them to.

Since their disbelief is only associating partners (shirk), and they also used to say "Allah," He said, expressing by what conveys the lowliness of everything other than Him: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, of lower rank than the ranks of the Supreme King, ﴿protectors﴾, that is, they hope that they will do with them what a close one does in benefit, defence and repelling. ﴿And for them﴾, along with His punishment, comes the frustration of their hope, ﴿is a great punishment﴾ which leaves no direction of theirs, no time of theirs, and no limb of theirs without filling it.

When He had informed of what awaits those who turn away from the signs, with that which is the most profound admonition and the most effective deterrent from misguidance, He said, pointing to what He opened the discourse with from the recited [revelation] of which this is a part: ﴿This﴾, i.e., the recited revelation upon you, ﴿is guidance﴾, i.e., very great, reaching [far] in guidance, and perfect in it. As for those who were guided by the signs of their Lord, [because] they were not deceived by the present, since it is transient, they used their intellects and so believed in it; for them is an enduring bliss. ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., concealed what the mirrors of their intellects showed them by it. This was the original form, but He drew attention to the fact that every sentence of it, indeed every word of it, is a clear indication of Him, glory be to Him, so He said: ﴿by the signs of their Lord﴾, i.e., and this covering is due to denying the signs that indicate the oneness of the One who does good to them. So they strayed from the way because of their neglect in reflection, through their delusion by the transient present. ﴿For them is a punishment﴾ existing ﴿of rijz﴾ [i.e., of retribution], filthy, very severe, of great agitation and turmoil, with consecutive movements. Al-Qazzaz said: al-rijz and al-rijs are one [and the same]. ﴿painful﴾, i.e., intensely painful. This verse is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one of two opposites is mentioned and the other is left to be understood, and vice versa): He mentioned guidance first as evidence for misguidance second, and disbelief and punishment second as evidence for their opposites first. Its secret is that He mentioned the cause of happiness to encourage it, and the cause of misery to deter from it.

The Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 45, verse 12:

When the Most Glorified and Most High mentioned the attribute of Lordship (rububiyyah), He mentioned some of its effects and of the signs (ayat) of His that are in it. So He said, resuming (musta'nifan) and indicating His greatness by the Greatest Name: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, who encompasses all attributes of perfection. And since the last of the signs He had previously mentioned was the winds, He mentioned what is disposed by directing them, so He said: ﴿Who subjected﴾, that is, He alone, without any power from you in that matter in any way whatsoever, ﴿for you﴾, O people, both the pious among you and the wicked, ﴿the sea﴾, with what He placed in it of things that none can determine except a single One with no partner, an agent acting by choice: its capacity for travel in it by its fineness, its softness and its evenness, together with the favorable wind, and that what is of wood floats upon it, along with what He knew of its craftsmanship in this manner by which the purpose was accomplished. ﴿That the ships may run﴾, that is, the vessels, ﴿therein by His command﴾, even if they were loaded with the weights of iron, which would sink, the lightest thing among it, such as a needle and what is less than it.

And since the implied meaning was: so that you may take heed by this and know that He is singularly by His power, so that you may believe in Him, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And that you may seek﴾, that is, you may seek, through the desire of the self and striving, by what you carry in it of merchandise, and that you may reach by it places and destinations, by hunting, diving and other means, ﴿of His bounty﴾, which none other than Him made or produced. And since the implied meaning was: so that the traces of His blessing may appear upon you, He joined to it His Exalted saying: ﴿And that you may be thankful﴾, that is, and that you may be in such a state that the one who observes your condition hopes from you that thankfulness, by which the One who bestowed His blessing upon you may increase you of His bounty in this world and the Hereafter.

When he had mentioned the sign of the sea for its greatness, he generalized to the benefits of the two horizons, indicating that He did not create all of that, despite its greatness, except for us. This alerts the reader that the matter is great. So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And He has subjected for you﴾, that is, exclusively, and had He willed, He could have prevented it. ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾, by sending it down to you, alerting that it is in a position where you cannot reach it in any way. He emphasized by repeating the relative pronoun, because the context is for indicating His might and wisdom, which indicate His oneness in deserving worship, a point they deny, just as they indicate His oneness in origination and sovereignty, which they acknowledge with their tongues, while their actions are the actions of one who denies it. So He said: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, and He connected you to it. Had He willed, He would have made you like what is in the heavens, with no way for you to reach it. He emphasized what the generality indicated before by His saying: ﴿all of it﴾, the state being that all of that is from the very essences of those things and from their subjection, ﴿from Him﴾, with no creation by anyone other than Him in any part of it in that regard. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': Abu Ya'qub al-Nahrajuri said: "He subjected all of it to you so that nothing from it would subject you, and you would be subjected to the One who subjected all of it to you, who is God, may He be exalted, for it is unseemly that the one served should serve his servant." (p. 77) Al-Qushayri said: "There is nothing among the visible essences except that it has, in some respect, a benefit for the human, so how could it subject you while it is itself subjected to you?"

When it was established that He has no partner in any part of creation, neither in essences nor in attributes, His saying, emphasizing it because their deeds contradict it, was very fitting: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in this great matter, which is His subjecting everything in the universe to us, ﴿are signs﴾, that is, clear indications that they, in turning to other than Him, are in manifest error, after He has subjected to us what we have of limbs and powers in this wondrous manner, even though among this which is subjected to us is what is stronger than us. ﴿for a people﴾, that is, people who have the capacity to undertake what is entrusted to them, ﴿who reflect﴾, that He alone deserves divinity, so that they do not associate anything with Him.

[p. 78] When the proofs of divine unity (tawhid, the oneness of God) had been made known in a manner from which it was understood that He has spread His blessings over all His creation, both the obedient and the disobedient, the excellent characteristics and praiseworthy actions became known through that. Since it is incumbent upon the one who turns toward Him and loves Him [to Him] to take on His attributes, He produced His saying, addressing the most understanding of His creation regarding Him and the most obedient of them to Him, to whom the commands are only [given] by way of His creative will (takwin), not of obligation, out of the intensity of their obedience: ﴿Say﴾, that is, by your speech and your state, ﴿to those who believe﴾, that is, those who claim to affirm everything that came to them from God: ﴿forgive﴾, following His example, those who have wronged you. Since this command is at the summit of requiring goodness toward the one who does evil, how much more so is pardoning him, it was as if it were an independent cause for turning toward Him, accepting from Him, and turning away from calling the wrongdoer to account, for that would detract from the perfection of turning toward Him. Moreover, whoever He (glory be to Him) wills to take vengeance upon, He suffices for his affair, and whoever He does not will that for, there is no way to restrain him, so occupying oneself with him is futile. He therefore drew attention to this by making the response to the command His saying ﴿they should forgive﴾, that is, they should cover over [the offense] with a thorough covering.

[p. 79] Since the intelligent person is one who strives with all his effort for the benefit of his own soul, and since harming the servants of God is a cause for expecting His anger and a detraction from what is hoped for of His goodness, He said ﴿to those who﴾, and in the place of "who have harmed them" He expressed it with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿do not expect﴾, that is, in reality and in metaphor. The expression in the place of fear (khawf) with hope (raja') is because of what it contains of enticement, encouragement, reconciliation, and seeking to win over. He said, after drawing attention to it through that expression, with a sublime allusion: ﴿the days of God﴾, that is, like [the] [p. 79] events of the Supreme King, who encompasses the attributes of perfection, among the past nations, through the alternation of dynasties, at one time in their favor and at another against them. In this is the greatest encouragement to urge pardon toward one who agrees in religion, and an admonition that no one proceeds to harm His servants except one who has turned away from Him. So his state becomes that of one who despairs of His (glory be to Him) acts of kindness in His recompense for the wrongdoer and the doer of good, in days and nights. He expressed it with the noble Name, as an alert to the majesty and beauty He possesses in dealing with each of them. Ibn Burjan said: this verse and those like it are of the "forgetting" mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever sign We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106]. It is not abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later one), but a ruling that comes and goes according to the capacity to prevail. Such [verses] used to descend in Makkah while the Muslims were weak, and after the Hijrah the verse of jihad and of enjoining what is right was revealed. These and their like were left recorded in the Qur'an because of what may come about of the turns of the days of God and of His days, the removal of the people of disbelief, as an admonition to the Muslims so that they might reconsider their affair and set right what is between them and their Lord.

[p. 80] Since whoever is requited for his offense in this world, the matter of it lapses for him in the Hereafter, and since the one who empowers the offender in reality is only God, exalted is He, and His empowering him was for profound wisdoms which will appear with utmost clarity in the Hereafter, He gave the reason for the command with forgiveness, threatening the offender and consoling the one wronged: ﴿That He may reward﴾, that is, God, in the reading of the majority with the yā' (third person) and the active voice; and "We" with what We have of greatness, in the reading of Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, with the nun (first person plural). Abu Ja'far made it passive, so that the deputy of the subject would be "the good or the evil," with the preposition elided, [reading as] "for their recompense" in this world and the Hereafter, where the ruling becomes manifest and injustice is made clear.

Since it may be that all the wrongdoers are recompensed, and it may be that some of them are pardoned through repentance or other means, as a favor for other wisdoms, and the one wronged is rewarded for his injustice in the same way, He said: ﴿a people﴾, that is, of the wrongdoers, even if they are at the utmost height of exaltedness, pride and tyranny, and of those wronged, even if they are at the utmost weakness, ﴿for what﴾, that is, by reason of which, ﴿they used to﴾, that is, in their natures and brought it out into the open, ﴿earn﴾, that is, they do, supposing that it benefits them, or by reason of their earning of good or evil. The sum is that He, exalted is He, says: turn away from the one who wronged you and leave his affair to Me, for I do not wrong you nor wrong anyone. So I will recompense you for your patience [p. 81] I will recompense him for his tyranny, and I am able to do so. The reading of Abu Ja'far conveyed the amplification in magnifying the agent, [showing] that He is known, and magnifying what has been put in its place, which is the recompense, by making it a principal and the predicate of it; for His greatness is in accordance with what has been put in its place. So the sense, given that the verb transitively takes two objects, is as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and He will reward them for what they endured with a garden and silk﴾ [al-Insan: 12]. That the Supreme King may recompense the supreme recompense of good to the believer and of evil to the disbeliever, a people. He made the recompense act like the subject, even though it is the object, just as "Zayd" is made the subject in "Zayd died," though it is the object in meaning, to draw attention to the great effect of the verb, for it is inseparable from it, since it is made capable of [reaching] the one recompensed [with the same firmness] as the one recompensed attains his recompense, and a refuge through it. For God, by the greatness of His power, makes a person's own deed his recompense. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿He will surely recompense them for their description﴾ [al-An'am: 139], according to what they used to do. It is also permissible that the deputy of the subject be the pronoun of "those who," by consideration of its wording, so the meaning would be: He will recompense those who believe [with] people who used to be powerful in standing against them in their harm, because of their harm to them [p. 81], so He makes each of them a ransom for each of them from the Fire. Perhaps they may see some traces of that in this world. Muslim and al-Tirmidhi related from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Charity does not decrease wealth, and God does not increase a servant through pardon except in honor, and no one humbles himself except that God, Mighty and Majestic, raises him." And Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, [p. 82] and the wording is his, and he said: "Hasan sahih," from Abu Kabshah al-Anmari, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Three things I swear by, and I will narrate to you a hadith, so memorize it: the wealth of a servant does not decrease by charity; no servant is wronged with an injustice and endures it except that God increases him in honor; and no servant opens a door of asking except that God opens for him a door of poverty," or a word similar to it. Al-Hakim related it and declared its chain sound. Al-Mundhiri said: there is a break in it. From Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may God be pleased with him, who said: "Whoever would like his building to be elevated for him and his ranks to be raised, let him pardon the one who wronged him, give to the one who denied him, and maintain ties with the one who severed them."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 15:

When Allah, glorified is He, had encouraged (to good) and warned (against evil), and it had been established that recompense is inevitable, He increased the encouragement and warning by stating that benefit and harm do not exceed them. So He said, explaining the recompense: ﴿Whoever does righteousness﴾, be it little or much, ﴿it is for his own self﴾, meaning the benefit of his deed is for himself alone; he will see its reward in this world or in the Hereafter. ﴿And whoever does evil﴾, meaning likewise, an evil, be it little or much, ﴿it is against himself﴾, meaning the harm of his evil deed is upon himself alone, likewise. This is most evident, for it is not conceivable to any rational person that a king would leave his servants without recompense, especially if he is wise, even though the deficiencies of souls have veiled this from many minds. Among its recompense is that the evildoer is made to prevail over the doer of good because of a slip that befell him, so that he may reconsider his condition through repentance.

Since Allah, glorified is He, is capable and nothing escapes Him, He is such that He does not hasten; so He postponed the recompense until the promised Day. ﴿Then﴾, meaning after being tested by being given respite in this world and detained in the barzakh, ﴿to your Lord﴾, meaning the One who alone owns you, not to anyone else, ﴿you will be returned﴾.

When he understood, through these wisdoms, what the surah opened with, namely that the One who sent down this Book is All-Mighty and All-Wise, the concluding summary (fadhlaka, a recapitulating conclusion) was: ﴿Indeed, We gave you the Book, the judgment and prophethood, and We favored you and your community over the worlds, and We sent you to warn people about what lies ahead of them.﴾ Since his people, after their agreement upon error, had differed over this Book, which should have brought them to firm unity and to seeking support through it, He followed this with words of consolation to him: ﴿And We certainly gave﴾, meaning, (p-84) by what We possess of greatness and overwhelming power, ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, the Prophet of God, your cousin Isaac, the Prophet of God, the son of your father Abraham, the friend of God, upon them be peace, ﴿the Book﴾, which comprises all good. It encompasses the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and others revealed to their prophets. ﴿And the judgment﴾, meaning knowledge and action that are firm in the way that rulings are firm, such that corruption cannot reach either of them, since knowledge gains adornment through action, and action gains perfection through knowledge. ﴿And prophethood﴾, through which great reports are known that people cannot access by any kind of acquisition on their own. Thus We made many prophets among them. ﴿And We provided them﴾ by Our greatness, for the sustenance of their bodies, ﴿with good things﴾, such as manna and quail and other provisions, both given directly and otherwise. ﴿And We favored them﴾ by what We possess of might, ﴿over the worlds﴾, meaning those whose existence We made certain in their time and before it. We gave them manifest and audible signs, and We made many prophets among them, which We did not do for others who came before them. All of this is a clear excellence.

﴿وآتَيْناهُمْ﴾ [And We gave them], despite this, ﴿بَيِّناتٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ﴾ [clear proofs concerning the matter], meaning the decisive proofs, rulings, and admonitions revealed to their prophets and confirmed by miracles, along with the attributes of the prophets who came after them and other matters that are in complete clarity for whoever We have decreed to be happy. This is a matter that calls for harmony and unity, and [qad] they were in agreement, even though they were in a time of misguidance (p-٨٥), and they did not differ except in a slight difference, the kind that does no harm and is not considered a difference.

Since their condition after this giving was general, He detailed it, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿فَما اخْتَلَفُوا﴾ [And they did not differ], that is, they brought about difference and division with their utmost effort. Since their difference did not encompass the whole period after the giving, He affirmed the qualifier and said: ﴿إلا مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ العِلْمُ﴾ [except after knowledge had come to them], which by its nature brings people together upon what is known. Thus, what was the cause of unity became for them a cause of division, because God, exalted is He, willed it, and He is the Mighty.

Since this is a wonder, he explained its cause, warning against its like, saying: ﴿بَغْيًا﴾ [out of rivalry], that is, transgressing the limits that the pursuit of leadership, envy, and other defects of souls had imposed on them. Since rivalry against an outsider is blameworthy, he increased its strangeness by saying: ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ [among themselves], occurring within them and not extending beyond them to others. Before that, while they were under the hand of the Qibt (Copts), they were in complete accord and unity of word in accepting humiliation. For this reason, he resumed with a statement that the situation required, in line with what the servants witness of the conduct of kings toward those who oppose their commands, emphasizing it to refute their denial: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ [Indeed your Lord], that is, the One who has been benevolent to you by sending you, multiplying your community, protecting them from what the earlier generations went astray in, and clarifying the Day of Decision, which is the seat of wisdom, with a clarification not given through the tongue of anyone among those who came before, ﴿يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ [will judge between them] by reckoning the deeds and recompensing them (p-٨٦), because this is what wisdom and might require, ﴿يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾ [on the Day of Resurrection], which your people deny, those whom We have honored with your messengership, although it is permissible in wisdom for it to be denied, ﴿فِيما كانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ [concerning that about which they used to differ], that is, concerning what had become like a disposition for them, with their utmost effort, deliberately intending it, unlike what occurred from them by error, for it is permissible in wisdom that He graciously pardon them for that. It is known that it is not at all permissible in wisdom to leave those who differ without a judgment between them, because even the least of kings would not accept this. The king is only recognized by dominance and might, and his wisdom is only recognized by justice. If a king does not accept this, how could the King of kings accept it? And if this judgment is required by wisdom, there is no distinction in it between one person and another, so it requires judgment between you as well in the same way. Among the emphasis on the promise of that Day is the expression of the name of the Lord with a pronoun attached to Him (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 18:

Since the meaning of this is that He, glorified and exalted, placed the Children of Israel upon a shari'ah (sacred law) and threatened them for opposing it, their threat became a threat to us. He said, explicitly stating what the flow of the discourse and other things require regarding our being threatened, and alerting to the loftiness of our shari'ah: ﴿Then﴾, that is, after an interval (fatrah) from their messengers and passing through many lofty ranks above the rank of their shari'ah, ﴿We placed you﴾, that is, by Our might, ﴿upon a shari'ah﴾, that is, a way (tariqah) that is broad, great, manifest, straight, easy, leading to the intended goal, worthy that people should begin to enter it and mix with it, ﴿of the affair﴾, which is Our revelation, and it is the life of spirits just as spirits are the life of bodies.

Since He, by this expression, clarified some of its excellence over what came before it, He made the following statement a consequence of it, addressing the Imam with what He intended for the followers, so that it would be more conducive to their striving, for their command is an obligation (taklif) while the command to their Imam is an act of bringing into being (takwin): ﴿So follow it﴾, that is, with the utmost of your effort. Since the shari'ah is the preserved intellect by which God, who informed us that He takes by it and gives by it, turning away from it to something else is only caprice (hawa). And since individuals of the community are not infallible, He alluded to pardoning their lapses by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not follow﴾, that is, do not deliberately follow ﴿the desires of those who do not know﴾, that is, those who have no knowledge, or who have knowledge but act like those who have no knowledge at all, from the disbelievers of the Arabs and others. For whoever deliberately follows them, I will do to them what I did to the Children of Israel, when I cursed them upon the tongue of David and Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon them both, after I had cursed them upon the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him,

(p-88) Then he gave the reason for this prohibition, threatening with his words [emphasizing, as an alert that whoever opposes God's command for the sake of someone is doing the deeds of one who thinks that person will protect him]: ﴿Indeed they﴾, and he emphasized the negation, so the Exalted said: ﴿will not avail you﴾, meaning: no kind of benefit that originates [from them] will come to them ﴿from God﴾, who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, reaching Him; and whatever has no connection to Him is nothing ﴿anything﴾ of benefit, if you follow them, just as they will not be able to harm you in any way if you oppose them and stand against them.

Since the implied meaning is: they are wrongdoers who do not place anything in its proper place, and whoever follows them is one of them, the Exalted said, linking to what precedes it: ﴿And indeed﴾. The original form would have been "and indeed they," but He used the explicit term to inform about their description, so He said: ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who are deeply immersed in this blameworthy attribute, ﴿some of them are allies of others﴾. So there is no alliance, that is, no nearness, between them and the Wise at all, because of the great distance between the two attributes. Therefore all their deeds were [entirely] void, since they were built on no foundation, unlike those who think otherwise of them, bound by the outward matters in this abode. ﴿And God﴾, that is, the One who possesses all attributes of majesty, beauty, might and perfection, ﴿is the ally of the God-fearing﴾ who are most concerned with attaining wisdom by taking the protective measures that save them from the wrath of God. (p-89) There is no alliance between Him and the wrongdoers.

When He, glory be to Him, had brought the explanation to this degree of clarity, which surpasses the capacities of humankind, He said, translating it: ﴿This﴾, that is, the revelation sent down. Because of the greatness of its clarity and its removal of confusion from every obscurity, whether subtle or obvious, such that nothing of ambiguity can reach it, He made it the very insight itself, expressed in the plural of abundance in the pattern of the final plural (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumū', the most extended plural form), just as He made it a spirit. So He said: ﴿insights for mankind﴾, that is, for those who are at the lowest ranks, it gives them insight into what harms them and what benefits them. So consider what it holds for those above them, among those who believe, and then those who have certainty, and those above them.

Having explained what it offers to the people of the lower ranks, He then explained what it offers to the people of the higher ranks, so the Exalted said: ﴿and guidance﴾, that is, a leader toward every good, a preventer from every deviation, ﴿and mercy﴾, that is, honour, success and blessing, ﴿for a people who have certainty﴾, that is, people in whom there is the strength to rise to firmly established knowledge and to renew their ascent through its degrees without any end, forever. Since the implication, after this explanation which has left no ambiguity regarding the matter of reckoning, in accordance with what He has defined of the King whose greatness and wisdom require that He call His servants to account, rewarding the good-doer and punishing the wrongdoer, is this: these addressees, because they can only be among the people or among those who have certainty through these insights, given the excellent natures that raise them from the depths of animality to the height of humanity, should know that We distinguish between the wrongdoers, some of whom are allies of one another, and the good-doers, whose allies We are. Then, glory be to Him and exalted, He followed this with His saying:

**Am** (a particle). Al-Asfahani said: The Imam said: "It is a word placed to ask about something when it is coordinated with another, whether the coordinated item is stated or implied." End of quote. The original wording would have been *hasibu* ("they reckoned"), but the text shifted away from it to alert the reader that committing evil blinds insight and weakens the intellect, as the expression *al-husban* ("reckoning") indicates, as was explained earlier in al-Baqarah. So He said:

﴿Do those who commit evil deeds reckon﴾, that is, those who did it with the utmost of their effort and the pull of their desires, ﴿that We will make them﴾, along with the greatness that is ours, which prevents injustice and requires wisdom, ﴿like those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, confirming their profession of faith outwardly and inwardly, secretly and openly, ﴿that We will leave them without accountability, since there is no distinction between the good-doer and the wrongdoer.﴾

Since the equality was stated in general terms, He clarified it by way of a new statement (*isti'naf*), placing first what is the very aim of the first sentence: ﴿equal﴾, that is, of great equality, ﴿their living and their dying﴾, that is, their lives and their deaths, and the time and place of these, in elevation and lowness, pleasure and distress, and other things, both concrete and abstract. Since this is something no one accepts for those under his authority, or for anyone else, He said, expressing it with a comprehensive term of blame: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is, their judgment has reached, in itself, the furthest extremes of wrongness, especially since they persist in it, renewing it every hour. It is therefore something to be wondered at, because the one who holds such a view does not know what drives him to it, for they ascribed to the Wise, who in reality has no wise one but Him, something that the least of people would not do toward those under his hand.

And when He denied equality and censured them for judging by it, He followed that with the decisive proof that the two groups are not equal—for otherwise the Creator of this existence would be neither Mighty (ʿAzīz) nor Wise (Ḥakīm). So He said, indicating the denial of equality and the evil of their judgment in it, consecutively upon what is implied by the context: "God created the heavens and the earth with truth." Truth is the established matter to which reality conforms, namely the permanence of the deeds of the good-doers and the nullity of the deeds of the wrongdoers. Then He joined to it His saying: ﴿And God created﴾, that is, the One to whom belong all attributes of perfection, and to whom no deficiency of any kind can attach or be conceived, ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, which are a receptacle for you, and with which the surah began by drawing attention to their signs, created ﴿with truth﴾, so that reality in them never conforms to anything false. (p-92) Whenever the cause of a thing exists and its impediment is absent, the thing exists; and whenever the impediment of a thing exists and its cause is absent, it does not exist. This never fails in any way. Therefore, the whole of what occurred in their creation conforms to the reality which is the power, knowledge and wisdom of God, and all the attributes of perfection which their creation indicates. If the receptacle is on this firmness, then what is to be assumed about what is contained, for whose sake the receptacle was created? Is it possible in wisdom that it be otherwise, so that the reality—which is the preference of the good-doer over the evildoer—would not conform to their conditions? Among what is contained between them is what is therefore not mentioned here. And if that were without resurrection and recompense according to deeds, this great creation would not be with truth but with falsehood, from which the Wise is exalted. How much more so, when He is the most just of judges.

And since the implication was: that every caused thing should conform to its causes, He followed it with His saying: ﴿That every soul may be recompensed﴾ [with the least of matters] ﴿for what﴾, that is, by means of the matter which ﴿it has earned﴾. Since the context is general, and the believer is only recompensed for what he did deliberately and intentionally in order that it be recorded in his deeds (p-93), He expressed it with "earning" (kasb), which is more specific than "doing" (ʿamal), saying: ﴿it has earned﴾, that is, its earning of good or evil; thus what was promised corresponds to its earning. ﴿And they﴾, that is, while they ﴿are not wronged﴾: no one brings about at any time a recompense for them not in its proper place. This is in accordance with what your customs of justice and grace have been. Had anything other than this come from Him, glorified is He, it would not be wrongdoing on His part, for He is the absolute Owner and the Supreme King. Were He to punish all the people of His heavens and His earth, He would not be unjust to them in reality. Thus this address is only according to what we are accustomed to in establishing proof by opposing the command.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 23:

When he had made clear the utmost of the clarity, that He is the sole God by virtue of His comprehensive possession of all the attributes of perfection, and that there must be a gathering of the creatures for the Day of Judgment (*Yawm al-Fasl*), to judge between them by His wisdom and power, and when he belittled desire (*hawa*) and forbade following it, and they had exalted it to the point of making it an object of worship, there followed from this the belittling of God by them, and they did not turn back from their error. From this there resulted a note of wonder at one who thinks that he is able (p. 94) to turn any of them back from their deviation by any means whatsoever. So He said: ﴿Have you seen﴾, that is, have you known with a knowledge that is, in its certainty, like what is perceived by the sense of sight, which is the most firmly established of the senses, ﴿him who takes﴾ [that is] with the utmost of his effort and striving ﴿his desire as his god﴾, that is, he has transformed the description of divinity until it became desire for his own self. So he is a follower of his desire and nothing more. He wanders in the valleys of error, not following any path, and so he is exposed to every affliction, and he has lost more than he gained, because he has no guidance.

The evidence that they worship nothing but mere desire is what al-Bukhari narrated in his *Sahih*, in the section on the expeditions (*maghazi*), concerning the delegation of Banu Hanifa, from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, who was a *mukhadram* (one who lived through both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods) and reliable (*thiqah*); he perceived the Jahiliyya and died in the year 105 AH at the age of 120 years. He said: "We used to worship stones. When we found a stone better than it, we would cast away the first and take the other. When we found no stone, we would gather a heap of dust, then bring a sheep and milk it over it, and then circumambulate it." End of quotation. Despite all of this, however you turn over their situation, you will find it to be a small branch of the disbelief of the *Ittihadiyya* (the monists who hold to the unity of existence), and every clinging of the Quraysh for which God reproached them has been clung to by the *Ittihadiyya*, even their saying: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us near to God in nearness﴾ [al-Zumar: 3].

Had he placed desire first, the meaning would be that he transformed its description into divinity, so desire vanished, and nothing remained but what is attributed to divinity (*al-Ilahiyya*), just as the clay vanishes in the phrase "the clay became one with the fire, so it became burnt." So the meaning becomes that the worshipper moves only in accordance with what God commands him. The structure (of the verse) conveys the exalting of Him by the predominance of affirmation and the removal of desire to the utmost of removal. And if the placing (of "desire" first) were, in this matter, according to the context without any difference in meaning, he would have placed "desire" here first, because the context and the preceding and following discourse are for it. And what is beneficial here has already been mentioned in Surah al-Furqan.

The second object of "ra'a" (to see/know) is omitted, and it is indicated by His saying at the end of the speech: ﴿Then who can guide him﴾. Its estimated meaning is: Is it possible for anyone other than God to guide him as long as his desire exists?

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "God did not mention desire in the Qur'an except that He condemned it." End of quotation. Its meaning is that it casts its owner down (*yahwi*) into the extended air, which is the open space, that is, it brings him down from a high rank to what is below it. So he is in a state of abasement as long as he follows it, because he is in a situation with no stability and no firm footing, and for this reason it entails humiliation. Al-Isfahani said: Ibn al-Muqaffa' was asked about desire (*hawa*), and he said: "It is humiliation (*hawan*) whose *nun* has been stolen." Then someone versified this, saying:

*The nun of humiliation from desire has been stolen,*
*and the captive of every desire is a captive of humiliation.*

And another said, not missing the meaning and excelling in it:

*Indeed desire is itself humiliation in its very essence,*
*so when you yearn (for it), you have met with humiliation.*

﴿And God has led him astray﴾, that is, by His comprehensive possession, ﴿knowingly﴾, from Him, with what He has created him upon: that there is no effect without an agent, and that there is no sole sovereignty except that the One who holds it deserves to be singled out for worship; and that He did not create the universe except by a Wise One, and that the Wise One does not leave those under His hand to oppress one another without judgment between them, especially since He has promised this, and especially since the promise of this is among the modes of the inimitability (*i'jaz*) with which they are most acquainted. Or (it means) "knowingly" on the part of the one who leads astray: that the one who is astray deserves this, because He created him with the nature of evil.

Since the one who is astray is in greater need of hearing the voice of the guide than of anything else, and since he who does not benefit from what he has is in the position of one who lacks it, He said: ﴿And sealed﴾, that is, in addition (p. 97) to the present leading astray, ﴿upon his hearing﴾, so he has no understanding of the verses that are heard. And since the deaf person may understand by gesture, He said: ﴿and his heart﴾, that is, so he does not comprehend what it is his duty to comprehend. And since the deaf madman may see his harms and benefits and then act upon them as animals do, He said: ﴿and placed upon his sight a covering﴾, so that he does not see the visible signs. Their order is thus because they are within the context of leading astray, as was mentioned earlier in al-Baqarah.

Since this human being has become one who does not hear the guide so as to turn to him, nor comprehend the meanings so as to benefit by what his knowledge has already given him, nor see with true sight so as to be guided by his sight, falling below the rank of an animal, the Exalted said, denouncing and making the denunciation a consequence of what preceded it: ﴿Then who can guide him﴾, and He indicated His power over him by His saying: ﴿after God﴾, that is, after the leading astray by the One who has comprehensive knowledge of everything. And since it is certainly known that there is no guide for him other than Him, He made the denunciation a consequence of their lack of remembrance, urging them toward remembrance, and so He said, indicating by the assimilation of the *ta'* of the *tafa''ul* form that there is no need, because of its clarity, for much (p. 98) remembrance: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾, that is, let there be for you some kind of remembrance, so that you remember that they do not hear the recited verses and do not take heed of the visible signs, despite the manifest clarity of each of them, and that for one whose state is this, there is no way for a creature like himself to guide him.

When the implied wording was for indicating the sealing over their faculties, they said, while acknowledging that He alone created them, provided their sustenance, and created all existing things, while denying His oneness, "He has partners." He linked to this his saying: ﴿And they said﴾, that is, in denying resurrection, while acknowledging that He is capable of everything and knowing that He has promised it in the miraculous discourses, and that it is not at all fitting for a wise One to leave those under His control to act lawlessly without judgment between them: ﴿It is nothing but our life﴾, that is, the life, ﴿the worldly life﴾, that is, this one in which we are, ﴿O people,﴾ and the mention of the implication of this description, which is a matter of forgetting that cannot be understood except in relation to another life after it, is sufficient to establish resurrection.

Having established, through their false claim, this life, they followed it with its condition, saying: (p-99) ﴿We die and we live﴾, that is, the soul is drawn out from some and they die, and it is breathed into others and they live, and there is no life after death for the one who has died. By this statement they stripped themselves of humanity and sank to the level of beasts, because they kept to particulars. Since their destruction, in their assumption, has no end, they regarded life as nothing in comparison with it, so they did not mention it and said, in their ignorance: ﴿And nothing destroys us﴾, that is, after this life, ﴿except time﴾, that is, the long span of time, through its dominance over us by the renewal of its favour and the renewal of our decline through the descent of disliked matters upon us, from "dahara" meaning he overcame him. When He attributed this feeble saying to them, He clarified their state at the point of their saying it, so the Exalted said: ﴿And not﴾, that is, they said it while the state was that they did not have ﴿for them in that﴾, that is, in that statement, far from correctness, which is that there is no life after this one, and that destruction is attributed to time as though it were itself the cause, ﴿any knowledge﴾, and he went to the extreme in negation and said: ﴿of it﴾, that is, much or little. ﴿They are only conjecturing﴾, that is, they are merely guessing, as evidenced by the fact that a person weakens as he advances in age, and that none of the dead has returned.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 25:

(p-100) Since this statement of theirs was a wonder, he (Allah) increased it in wonder by their condition upon hearing the decisive proofs. So He said, conjoining it to "they say": ﴿And when Our verses are recited﴾, i.e., are followed up with recitation by whoever recites them, ﴿to them﴾, i.e., with what they possess of greatness in themselves and by their being attributed to Us, ﴿as clear evidences﴾, i.e., in the utmost capacity of indicating the resurrection, so they have no excuse for rejecting them, ﴿their argument is not﴾, i.e., in any aspect of being, ﴿but that they say﴾, i.e., their statement which they put forward as if it were an argument, and which does not deserve to be called even a doubt, ﴿[except] "Bring forth our fathers"﴾, i.e., the dead ones. That is, the sum of this is that they had no argument except that they produced a statement whose meaning is: "We have no argument," for it contains not even a doubt, let alone an argument. Their calling themselves ignorant did not suffice them, until they confronted the people of the clear evidences with falsehood and said: ﴿If you are truthful﴾, i.e., firmly established in the matter among the people of truthfulness who are steadfast in it, that He, glorified and exalted, raises the creation after their death. And this is a declaration of far-fetchedness on their part that He could be able to gather the body after it has decayed, while they acknowledge that He is the One who created that body in the first place. (p-101) And it is known with certainty that whoever is able to originate something from nothingness is all the more able to restore it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 26:

Since Allah, glorified and exalted, accepts faith only when it is possible to conceive of it, and that is when it is through the unseen, He did not answer them concerning the raising of their fathers, out of honour for this community because of the nobility of its Prophet, upon him be the best of prayers and peace. For His divine practice (sunnah) has proceeded that whoever does not believe after the matter has been made manifest through the bringing about of the suggested signs, He destroys, as He did with the earlier nations. So He lifted them from the sensory to training in rational proofs, and He said, commanding him (ﷺ) to answer, with His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power, knowledge and wisdom, ﴿gives you life﴾, that is, He renews this renewal without end, just as you acknowledge it, bringing to life bodies which He originates without there being any root of life in them. ﴿Then He causes you to die﴾, by gathering your spirits from your bodies and drawing them out of them, leaving not "anything" of them in any part of the body. That is not difficult for Allah, and then it is as it was before the giving of life, as you witness. Whoever is able to originate this in this manner of repetition, and then to distinguish the spirit that was dispersed when it is drawn out of those visible organs, in a constant habitual manner, is the one who reports truly, of the two groups, that He gathers creation after their death. Therefore He said, without emphasis: ﴿Then He will gather you﴾, that is, after dispersal, so He returns your spirits into you as they were after a long duration of sleep, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, the Great Rising, because it is general to all creatures whom He caused to die.

When the claim was established by this decisive proof, He produced His saying: ﴿There is no doubt﴾, that is, no doubt in any respect ﴿concerning it﴾, rather it is known with certain, necessary knowledge. ﴿But most of mankind﴾, by reason of the baseness they have, through what We have placed in them of appetites and desires which overcame the natural disposition of reason, so they were returned by them to the lowest of the low, within the limit of oscillation, which is vacillation, ﴿do not know﴾ [i.e., no knowledge renews for them, because of their oscillation, vacillation and descent] from the zenith of reason to the nadir of ignorance. They stand fixed with sensible things, and that matter does not shine for them, though it has such clarity, so that Our power may be manifest and Our hidden name be realized, just as the manifest is realized for those whom We have guided, for the knowledge of this.

To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. (Allah) having shown His power to bring back (creation) by this particular proof, whose implied sense is: "Allah, who initiated your creation from the earth in this manner, is capable of restoring you," He followed it with another comprehensive proof, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, the Supreme King alone, ﴿the dominion of the heavens﴾ in their entirety, ﴿and the earth﴾ from which He initiated you. Whoever disposes of anything in His dominion is capable of its like, so long as he is a king.

Since the implied meaning is: "To Him belongs the dominion of that forever; He does in it today what you witness, raising this and lowering that. Had people submitted to His decree, they would have attained everything they attained through tyranny and transgression, for nothing goes beyond His command. But most people today are in doubt, hesitating," He built upon it His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, that is, it comes into existence and is realized with the realization of one who stands, in full command of his affairs, perfectly capable and rising to bear the burdens of what he wills. And He, glory be to Him, repeated for emphasis and to instill awe, His saying: ﴿on that day﴾, that is, when the Hour is established, they will lose. This was originally the wording, but He said it for generality and to attach the description: ﴿the falsifiers will lose﴾, that is, those who enter into falsehood and are deeply immersed in characterizing themselves by it, who would not accept My decree, so they hasten and reach their aims by means I did not command. They continue to transgress until the time arrives that I have decreed for their attainment (of those aims), and they attain them, thinking that they attained them by their own striving, and that had they been left alone, they would not have had that. Thus they lose through their striving, because of the choice I granted them to pursue My will concerning them in opposition to My command, a loss that is continually renewed, from which they have no escape. But the people of truth will triumph.

When that day was so terrifying, he generalized the terror, depicting its state with his words: ﴿And you will see﴾, that is, on that day, ﴿every nation﴾ of the nations, both those who will be lost therein and those who will succeed, ﴿kneeling﴾, that is, gathered together with no one else mixed among them. Yet, along with that, they will be crouching on their knees, out of terror and readiness for whatever they may be commanded, in the posture of an adversary before the judge, awaiting the final judgment and the decisive, binding command, because of the severity of the terror of that day that will appear to them. And since it was as if it had been said, "They will be poised and alert," he said: ﴿every nation﴾ (p-105), that is, from among those kneeling, ﴿will be called to its record﴾, that is, the book that was sent down to it and by which Allah imposed worship upon it, and also the record the guardian angels have copied of its deeds, so that each of the two may be matched against the other. Whoever's record agrees with what was commanded in the Book of his Lord will be saved, and whoever opposes it will perish. And it will be said to them at the time of the call: ﴿Today you will be recompensed﴾ according to wisdom, with the easiest of matters, ﴿for what﴾, that is, the very thing that ﴿you used to do﴾ with that which is innate to you, as though it were part of your nature, ﴿working﴾, that is, persisting in it without turning back from it, [whether] good or evil.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 29:

When He had informed them of the recompense, He explained the manner by which the Book of Revelation (*kitab al-inzal*) and the Book of Deeds (*kitab al-a'mal*) are matched against one another. What the Book of Revelation has judged, the Great, the Exalted, enforces. So He said, pointing to the Book of Revelation with the demonstrative for the near because of its nearness and the ease of understanding it: ﴿This is Our Book﴾ [i.e.] which We sent down upon the tongues of Our messengers, ﴿speaking﴾, i.e., bearing witness with a testimony that in its clarity is like speech, ﴿against you with truth﴾, i.e., with the established matter that corresponds to the reality of your deeds. That is, it says: whoever does such-and-such is an unbeliever, whoever does such-and-such is a disobedient one, and whoever does such-and-such is an obedient one. It then matches this against what you have done, so that what the Book has reported corresponds to your deeds, with neither addition nor deficiency. Every universal corresponds to its particulars exactly, just as We will give you knowledge of this on that Day, so the reality of your natures is disclosed and every particular of your actions that occurred from you, not even an atom of it escaping. You will know that this reality which occurred from you corresponds (p-106) to what the Book We sent down reported, so it is true, because the reality conformed to it. This is its speaking against you. As for its speaking for you, it is the bounty: the good deed is rewarded tenfold, and more than that.

Since the custom in this world is that rights are upheld by writing documents, and since they were as if saying, "Who will preserve our deeds despite their multitude, the long duration and the distance of time?", and since they were denying the matter of the guardian angels and other things that the messengers brought, He emphasized His statement, answering in a way that brings it closer to the understanding of one who asks about this: ﴿Indeed We﴾, with the power and the majesty We possess, free from any need for writing, ﴿were﴾ continually ﴿having copied﴾, i.e., commanding Our angels to transcribe any transmission, ﴿what you used to﴾ do by nature and disposition ﴿do﴾ in word, deed and intention. If the meaning of "copying" is general transmission, this is clear. If the transmission is from an original, then it refers to the tablet of natures indicated by "you used to," or to the Preserved Tablet, so that it matches what the doer does. It is well known among people that everyone has written on his forehead whatever good or evil he encounters.

(p-107) When he had explicitly stated the case of the falsifiers, according to what the context required, as was mentioned earlier, and had alluded to the truthful, he stated explicitly what he had hinted at concerning the matter of [the truthful] and [coupled] their opposites with them. He said, beginning with them in the manner of *al-nashr al-mushawwash* (the disordered arrangement, in which items are listed in a different sequence from the order in which they were introduced) in detail: ﴿As for those who believed﴾, that is, from among the kneeling nations, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, confirming their claim of faith, ﴿their Lord will admit them﴾, that is, on that Day whose greatness and severity of terror we have mentioned, ﴿their Lord﴾, who was gracious to them by granting them success in righteous, pleasing deeds that lead to Him, ﴿into His mercy﴾, that is, into His nearness and honour, with sublime reward and a good return. The angels will say to them, as an honour: "Peace be upon you, O believers." He indicated the magnitude of the mercy by His saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, this exalted favour, ﴿is﴾ [that is] not other than it, ﴿the triumph﴾.

Since the context concerned their dullness and the obscurity of things to them, He said, exalted is He: ﴿the Manifest﴾, He whose matter is not hidden from anyone, since nothing of it is mixed with turbidity or deficiency at all, unlike what was among its causes in this world, for these, despite being a triumph, were very obscure to those who were not certain.

﴿وأمّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ As for those who disbelieved, that is, they concealed what the polished mirrors of their intellects and their original natural dispositions (fitar) had made clear to them of the truth that God commanded, even if they did all the righteous deeds other than faith. So the Supreme King will admit them into His curse.

Since this concealment was a clear cause of their rebuke, He said: ﴿أفَلَمْ﴾ Did not.
