That is, it will be said to them: Did not My messengers come to you, and did I not create for you intellects that guide you to what is right, through reflecting upon the visible signs of the miracles they brought you, and did I not send down upon you, through them, audible signs? But ﴿تَكُنْ آياتِي﴾ My signs were not [recited to you], despite their great dignity in being attributed to Me, and despite the great dignity of their coming to you on the tongues of My messengers, who are the noblest of My creation.

Since these signs necessitate faith by virtue of their greatness, merely by being recited, the verb is put in the passive: ﴿تُتْلى﴾ are recited, that is, their recitation is continued by whatever reciter it may be. How much more so when they are conveyed through the messengers, as a recitation that is exalted ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ over you, which you cannot repel by anything that a fair-minded person would accept. ﴿فاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ Then you became arrogant. That is, from the recitation of these signs, which by their nature produce humility, submission and lowliness, there resulted your seeking arrogance for yourselves, and you brought it into being against My messengers and My signs. ﴿وكُنْتُمْ﴾ And you were, as a settled trait (khuluqan lazimal), ﴿قَوْمًا﴾ a people, that is, possessing standing and capacity for what you attempt, ﴿مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ criminals, that is, deeply persistent in severing what deserves to be joined. That is the manifest loss.

This verse is an example of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which each of two contrasting parts is left implicit and understood from the other): it mentions admission into mercy first as an indication of admission into curse second, and mentions the rebuke second as an indication of the honouring first. Its secret is that what it mentions is more indicative of the nobility of the beloved (waliyy) and the baseness of the enemy.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 32:

﴿And when﴾, that is: and when you are told, by whatever speaker it is said, even if it is said for emphasis, ﴿"Indeed, the promise of God"﴾, which everyone knows encompasses the attributes of perfection, ﴿"is true"﴾, that is: established, with no deviation from it, and reality corresponds to it regarding the Resurrection and other matters, because even the least of kings would not be content to have his promise broken, so how much more so God, glorified and exalted be He, and how much more so when breaking a promise would contradict wisdom. ﴿"And the Hour"﴾, which is among the things He promised, and is the locus of wisdom, is the greatest matter to which the promise relates (p-110) ﴿"there is no doubt about it"﴾ in any respect, because it is the place where the sovereignty is manifested in the most complete way, with its majesty and beauty. ﴿You said﴾, content with yourselves in the depths of ignorance: ﴿"We do not know"﴾, that is, now, with the knowledge of certainty, even if we exerted our effort in seeking to reach it, ﴿"what the Hour is"﴾, that is: we do not know its reality, let alone what you tell us of its conditions.

Since its matter is fixed in the natural dispositions and does not require great reflection, by what everyone knows of the perfect power of God, whenever it is alerted to it in any manner, knowledge of it comes to the heart. They called that mere conjecture, out of obstinacy and arrogance, and so they said, beginning a response to one who seems to say: Has the recitation of these clear verses not conveyed knowledge of it to you? ﴿"Indeed"﴾, that is: we ﴿"only suppose"﴾, that is: we believe what you tell us about it, ﴿"a supposition"﴾, but as for its reaching the level of knowledge, no. Since the restricted element (al-ḥaṣr, restriction) must necessarily be more specific than the element it restricts, the first "supposition" means belief. Perhaps he expressed it with the term "supposition" to emphasize the meaning of restriction. For this reason they joined to it, explicitly stating the intended meaning, since "supposition" may also be used for knowledge, their statement: ﴿"And we are not"﴾, and they emphasized the negation, saying: ﴿"certain"﴾, that is: there is no certainty about its matter present with us, nor are we seekers of it (p-111). This is alongside what you witness of the signs [in the horizons and in yourselves, and what He disperses of living creatures, and what alerts you to that among the signs] that are heard, and this does not contradict [the verse]: ﴿"There is only our life of this world"﴾, because its ending affirms supposition. It seems that they were at times strengthened by what was in their innate constitutions and original natures regarding its matter, so they supposed it; and at other times their appetites prevailed over them together with the doubt that accompanies them, which is founded on ignorance, so they supposed its non-existence and were certain of it, because of the soul's inclination toward it. Or they were two groups. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 33:

When they reached a great degree of obstinacy, He turned to the mode of the third person (al-ghayba), turning away from them, as a notice of intense anger. So the Exalted said: ﴿And there will appear﴾, meaning: they did not cease saying that until the Hour appeared to them with what it contains of terrors, quakes and horrors, and there became manifest ﴿to them﴾ in the utmost manifestation ﴿the evil deeds of what﴾. Since the context concerns the disbelievers, and they were being held accountable for all their deeds, for they have no sound foundation that could be a cause for the expiation of anything of what they engaged in, and since the context did not specifically require something like "the sins" (al-zumar), he expressed it with "deeds" (al-'amal), which is more general than "earning" (al-kasb), so he said: ﴿they did﴾. Thus there was displayed to them [the consequences of their deeds], they knew the measure of their recompense, and they became aware of everything that follows from that. ﴿And there encompassed them﴾, meaning: it surrounded them in a state of subjugation and overpowering. Abu Hayyan said: it is not used except for what is disliked.

﴿That which they used to﴾ by disposition and character ﴿mock at﴾, meaning: they produced mockery of it with the utmost appetite and pleasure, as one who is eager for it.

﴿And it will be said﴾, that is, to them, at the most severe and final moment, a word with no one to follow it up, as if it were spoken by the tongue of every speaker: ﴿Today We forget you﴾, that is, We will deal with you by abandonment, withholding from you all that would set you right, the treatment given to one who is forgotten, whom We cut off from all Our kindness, so that every evil befalls him, ﴿as you forgot﴾. He attached the verbal noun (al-masdar) to its time-frame (zarf) for the elegance and eloquence this carries, saying: ﴿the meeting of this your day﴾, that is, the day for whose affair you acted as one who forgets it. Whoever forgets the meeting of the Day has forgotten the meeting of what happens in it, all the more so. Allah, glorified and exalted, has blamed them for this with the utmost blame (p-113), because what they did is not the behaviour of the prudent (al-hazamah, "those of sound judgement"), who would not abandon something whose harm is possible while giving it no regard. Rather, this is the behaviour of fools whom they regard as worthless (asqal, "dregs"), having no consideration or weight. He expressed it by forgetting because their knowledge of it is fixed in their natures. He expressed their action in the present tense to indicate continuity, and their act in the past tense to indicate that whoever does this at any time, even briefly, has put himself in great peril by exposing himself to the continuing turning away from it.

Since leaving them in this state entails the continuance of punishment, He stated it explicitly as a clarification, lest anything else be supposed, saying, describing their condition: ﴿And your abode is the Fire﴾, meaning you have no escape from it at all, because your deeds brought you into it, and no one comes out of it except one whom We permit to come out. We have placed you among those who are forgotten, so there will be no relief (faraj) for you from Us. ﴿And you have no﴾, in reality, whether you reflected on defending against this day or whether you abandoned it in the manner of one forgotten, ﴿helpers﴾ who will rescue you from that by intercession or by overpowering force.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 35:

When He mentioned their recompense, which is the truth matching their deeds, a retribution exactly corresponding to the act, He gave the reason for it by what their deeds necessarily entailed, and said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the great punishment, ﴿because you took﴾, i.e., by your own imposition upon yourselves and your forcing of yourselves against what reason has led to, what the Messengers brought, and what the primordial natures (al-fitar al-uwal) have assented to, ﴿the signs of God﴾, i.e., the Great King, than whom nothing is greater, ﴿a mockery﴾, i.e., you made them the very opposite of what I sent down, for the sake of keeping away from it. ﴿And the worldly life deceived you﴾ because of the weakness of your minds, ﴿the worldly life﴾, i.e., the lowly one, so you preferred it because it is present, while you were like cattle whose perception does not go beyond what is sensed. So you said: "There is no life other than this, and no resurrection, and no reckoning." Had you reasoned about its description, it would have led you to acknowledge the other life.

When He had brought them to this degree of humiliation, He made the following a consequence of it, as an increase in their humiliation, a delight for His allies whom they had opposed in this, and a gloating over them: ﴿So today﴾, after being lodged in it, ﴿they will not be brought out﴾ by any means ﴿from it﴾, because God does not bring them out, and no one other than Him is able to do so. ﴿Nor will they be asked﴾ specifically ﴿to make amends﴾, i.e., it will not be sought from them by any seeker that they make i'tab, which is apologizing with what establishes their excuse and removes from them the blame (al-atab) that calls forth anger, by means of any of the righteous deeds, because they are in the abode of recompense, not the abode of action.

Then, after establishing—by means of the visible and audible signs, the exalting of His allies, and the humbling of His enemies—that He (glory be to Him) acts without concern for anything and is never incapable of anything, with complete encompassing knowledge and power of all things, there necessarily follows from this His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So to Allah﴾, i.e., He to whom the whole command belongs, ﴿belongs all praise﴾, i.e., the comprehensive attribution of all the qualities of perfection. And when He (glory be to Him) made clear that this belongs to Him by His very essence and not by anything else, He established that it is not by beneficence and management alone, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens﴾, i.e., the One possessing elevation, vastness and blessings. And since the context is to establish exclusivity in perfection, and they had assigned to Him (glory be to Him) partners in a way that indicated that they had no basis for their worship, restricting their affair to whim, He repeated the mention of the Lord as emphasis and as an informing that He has in each of the two regions (al-khafiqayn) secrets different from those in the other, so the nurturing varies according to that. He also introduced the conjunction to inform that the perfection of His power in His lordship over the higher and the lower is on one and the same level, repelling the supposition that His rule is more feasible in the higher realm, due to the supposition of need for a distance; so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and Lord of the earth﴾, i.e., the One possessing receptivity to what comes upon it.

And when He singled out the two regions, drawing attention to reflection upon the signs contained in them because of their manifestness, He generalized, as an alert that beyond that He has creatures that none knows except Allah (glory be to Him, exalted is He), so He said, dropping the conjunction because there is no need for it after establishing the equality of the two realms, the higher and the lower, in His rule with respect to knowledge and power, for the sake of transcendence above distance: (p-116) ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾. So He gathered together a term whose singular applies to all originated things, because "the world" (al-'alam) is everything other than Allah—as an alert to its categories and an explicit statement of them, and an informing that what is meant by it is its primary (muṭābaqī) signification, not a part of it by implication (tadammun). He repeated the mention of the Lord as an alert that His preserving the creation and His nurturing them takes many forms according to the affairs of creatures: His preserving this part is in a manner different from His preserving another part, and His preserving the whole insofar as it is a whole is in a manner different from His preserving each part individually, although the whole is equal in relation to His complete power.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 45, verse 37:

When this established His absolute self-sufficiency (ghina), His lordship (siyada), and that there is no equal to Him, He followed it with some of its necessary implications, to draw attention to the great care that must be given to it, in order to repel what they imagine of ascribing partners to Him, which [not] they would accept for themselves. So He said: ﴿And to Him﴾, that is, to Him alone, ﴿belongs greatness﴾, that is, the supreme magnificence that has no end, ﴿in the heavens﴾ all of them ﴿and the earth﴾ all of it, the two in which there are signs for the believers. Muslim, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from Abu Hurayrah, and Muslim from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Greatness is My cloak and majesty is My garment, so whoever contends with Me over either of them, I shall cast him into the Fire." In another narration: "I shall punish him," and in another: "I shall break him."

﴿And He﴾, alone, is ﴿the Almighty﴾, who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything, ﴿the All-Wise﴾, who places things in their most perfect positions and does not place anything except in that manner, just as He perfected His command, His prohibition, and all of His law. He also perfected the arrangement of this Qur'an in its sentences and verses, its closing rhyme-words (fawasil) and its ends, and after He made its meanings and its revelation exact as a response to what they were concerned with, it became miraculous in its arrangement, its meaning, and its sending down, fitting the answers to the events as the situation required. Thus its last part corresponds to its first part through the two attributes mentioned, and through its exhortation to reflect upon the signs of the two horizons, and through its explicit statement of what follows from that of greatness, which requires the humbling of enemies and the honoring of allies. And Allah is the Guide to what is right, and to Him is the return and the final destination. And Allah knows best His intended meaning.
